source: Royal Government of Cambodia, General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA) / Boosting Food Production Program (PMO), "ខែ្សសង្វាក់ផលិតកម្ម ដំណាំពោតនៅកម្ពុជា" (Corn Production Value Chain in Cambodia), 2017
text:
The document describes five broad groups of actors who supply inputs and services to red-corn farmers, functioning together in the value chain:

1. Seed suppliers -- can be community/village-based farmers reselling seed they've kept, or dedicated seed retailers, often selling seed of unverified quality with no formal grading or certification.

2. Fertilizer and pesticide/agrochemical sellers -- the largest of the five input-supplier groups. These are typically licensed retailers whose products are subject to some quality/safety oversight, though farmers report inconsistent trust in product quality and correct application guidance.

3. Farm machinery/equipment providers -- includes farmers who own tractors or other equipment and hire them out to neighbors, and dedicated service providers offering land-preparation or harvest machinery for rent.

4. Corn collectors/traders -- buy corn from farmers, either wet (fresh cob) or dried (shelled kernel), and transport it onward to district or provincial markets or to the export border. There are two sub-types: collectors who buy specifically for the Cambodian domestic market, and collectors who buy specifically to resell for export.

5. Exporters and large buyers (including feed mills and border traders) -- move product either to domestic feed mills or across the border, mainly to Vietnam and Thailand, and to a smaller but growing degree to China.

The document notes limited coordination and formal contracting between these groups -- most transactions are informal/spot-market, with farmers generally lacking binding forward contracts with buyers, which contributes to price volatility and uncertainty for farmers at harvest time.
